notes: Polite, neutral register for a modern Thai app: no gender-specific particles (ครับ/ค่ะ); address the user as “คุณ” only where a pronoun is needed, otherwise omit it; use “โปรด” for requests. Labels and buttons are short nouns/verbs. Thai has no capitalisation. No full stops at the end of sentences: separate sentences and clauses with a single space instead, and render English “ — ” in messages as a space (e.g. “บันทึกไม่สำเร็จ โปรดลองอีกครั้ง”); keep “?” on direct questions, keep “:” and “…”/“...” as in the English. Quotation marks are curly “ ”. Write “อื่น ๆ” with spaced ไม้ยมก. Use Arabic numerals. Loanwords follow Royal Institute spelling where common (เวอร์ชัน, อัปโหลด, ลิงก์, ฟอนต์). Option names that Lulu or Google Fonts show only in English stay in English.
